The image shows a jammed, over-equioscillated optimum: over 350 pairs are tied within $10^{-16}$ of the maximum, every point has 23--44 contacts, and there are zero rattlers. With $59\cdot21=1239$ tangent degrees of freedom (1008 after quotienting by $SO(22)$ rotations), that dense contact graph is over-rigid, so no first-order tangent or LP direction can lower all contacts, tiny Gaussian shakes are reabsorbed, and repeated dense LPs merely spend the time limit certifying local optimality. The missing structural property is slack heterogeneity—a substantially sparser contact set, a low-contact or rattler subset, and a different active-pair topology that permits coordinated many-point motion.
